subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a CLI-visible global agent dry-run mode, and what no-side-effects guarantee should it make across embedded tools, Gateway fallback, CLI-native/client-hosted tools, and plugin hooks?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the requested mode creates a user-trusted security boundary whose scope cannot be inferred safely from existing scoped dry-run commands or plugin hook behavior.

options.title: Approve a narrow dry-run contract first
options.body: Define CLI-only v1 semantics, including what still runs for model/auth/setup and how client/native tools are reported, then allow a bounded implementation.

options.title: Broaden into safe workflow modes
options.body: Fold this into the wider ask/plan/modify product direction so dry-run becomes one named mode in a larger execution-control design.

options.title: Reject core mode for now
options.body: Keep using scoped command dry-runs and plugin hooks, accepting that there is no built-in global agent preview guarantee.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow dry-run contract first
recommendation.body: Define CLI-only v1 semantics, including what still runs for model/auth/setup and how client/native tools are reported, then allow a bounded implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to broad agent-runtime ownership and recent security/product routing work in the relevant execution surface.
